evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.limitation: The scenario definition (champions, levels, roster composition, target resistances, event ordering) lives outside data/ and outside docs/math-foundations.md, so the absolute damage number is not reconstructible from the permitted evidence. The computation below is therefore a RATIO oracle: it identifies the exact sourced quantity that separates 94.1 from 101.7 and rules the direction.

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json — corpus-wide decoding of the wiki {{rd|A|B}} template (melee value first, ranged value second)
sources_quoted.quote: Ravenous Hydra {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}} · Titanic Hydra {{rd|4%|2%}} · Blade of the Ruined King {{rd|9%|6%}} · Divine Sunderer {{rd|6%|4%}} — in every legendary the second (ranged) value is the reduced one, fixing Bloodsong's split as melee 8% / ranged 5%.

Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md §2.1 (resistance identity, used to bound the Black Cleaver alternative)

sources_quoted.quote: Black Cleaver average stacks (`ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction`): the established model uses a fixed `0.8·max_stacks` constant ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C`

sources_quoted.source: data/atoms/autoresearch-review.md §3.2 and §4 (pair-fight / roster coupling; the historical gap class)
sources_quoted.quote: each pair fight cannot see the roster, so the engine authors the full value with an explicit reduced receipt; the coupled ledger re-prices defenders past the first (`defender_index > 0`)  ...  plus execute branches (Pantheon Q, Shaco E, Naafiri recast) and damage-mod debuffs (Vladimir R amp, Wukong Q shred).

step_1_observed_ratio.note: Golden leaves are stored to one decimal, so the true multiplier lies in [101.65/94.15, 101.75/94.05] = [1.07945, 1.08188].

step_2_candidate_from_the_cache.quantity: Bloodsong 'Expose Weakness': target takes 8% (melee holder) increased damage from ALL sources for 4 s
step_2_candidate_from_the_cache.check: 94.1 x 1.08 = 101.628; with the golden's 1-decimal storage the underlying pre-amp value must lie in [94.1204, 94.15) for the amped result to print 101.7 (e.g. 94.14 x 1.08 = 101.6712 -> 101.7). Both printed values are simultaneously consistent with exactly one factor of 1.08.
step_2_candidate_from_the_cache.why_multiplicative: data/wiki-atoms/damage.json: percent damage modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based mitigation, so an 8% amp is a clean scalar on the post-mitigation pair damage regardless of where in the pipeline it is applied.

step_3_ranged_variant_rejected.verdict: rejected — 94.1 x 1.05 = 98.81, nowhere near 101.7; the engine used the melee (8%) leg of {{rd|8%|5%}}.

carve_stack_model_change_24pct_to_30pct.verdict: rejected — physically impossible. The whole 24%->30% band is bounded above by 0.76/0.70 = 1.0857 only as armor -> infinity; at any realistic armor (60-200) it buys at most ~3-5%, not 8.1%. So the leaf did NOT move because the Black Cleaver averaging constant was swapped for the Cesaro mean C - C(C-1)/(2h).

carve_newly_propagated_to_the_pair_0pct_.verdict: numerically possible but parameter-tuned; it needs the defender's post-penetration armor to land on 45.2 (or 33.2 for a full 30% shred). The Expose Weakness explanation needs no free parameter at all — it predicts 1.08 exactly. Occam favours the amp; and both readings share the same direction (a sourced roster-visible debuff that pair damage was previously missing).

step_5_direction_ruling.question: Does event 28's pair damage carry zero or one factor of Expose Weakness?
step_5_direction_ruling.wiki_rule: 'causing them to take 8% increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES' — the debuff is a property of the TARGET, not of the Bloodsong holder's own damage. In a coupled roster fight, a pair-damage event landing on an Expose-Weakness-flagged defender within the 4 s window must be amplified once, whoever the attacker is.
step_5_direction_ruling.timing: The debuff arms after the first empowered (Spellblade) basic attack and refreshes on a 1.5 s cooldown for 4 s. Event index 28 is deep into the timeline, long past the first ability + empowered attack, so the window is open at that event.
step_5_direction_ruling.prior_state_of_the_engine: data/atoms/autoresearch-review.md's swarm synthesis lists 'damage-mod debuffs' as an open unmodeled/mis-modeled class, and §3.2 records that a pair fight 'cannot see the roster' — i.e. exactly the failure mode in which a roster-mate's Expose Weakness would be dropped from another participant's pair damage. 94.1 is that un-amplified number; 101.7 = 94.1 x 1.08 restores the sourced debuff.
step_5_direction_ruling.conclusion: 101.7 carries exactly one factor of the wiki-sourced 8% melee Expose Weakness amplification; 94.1 carries none. The cache says the amplification is owed.

residual_assumptions: The Bloodsong holder in this roster is MELEE. The observed ratio is the melee leg (8%) of {{rd|8%|5%}}; if the scenario's Bloodsong carrier is a ranged champion, the sourced amp would be 5% and BOTH values would be wrong (correct value ~98.8). The scenario definition is outside the permitted evidence tree, so this could not be checked; the pairing of Bloodsong with Black Cleaver (a melee-fighter item) in the same scenario makes a melee carrier the strongly favoured reading.

The debuffed defender at event 28 is the champion that actually received the empowered attack. Expose Weakness is inflicted per-target; amplifying a defender who was never hit by the Spellblade attack would be an over-application. Nothing in data/ contradicts the single-application reading, and the ratio is exactly one factor of 1.08 either way.

Symmetry note: a 1 -> 2 double-application bug would produce the same 1.08 ratio with the old value correct. That reading is disfavoured because the cache-documented gap class is missing damage-mod debuffs, not duplicated ones, and because a debuff that a pair fight 'cannot see' is the documented coupling failure mode.
verdict_rationale: The leaf moved by exactly one factor of 1.08 — the melee value of Bloodsong's Expose Weakness, quoted verbatim from data/items.json, which the wiki states applies to damage 'from all sources' on the flagged target. Every Black Cleaver explanation is either arithmetically impossible (the 24%->30% averaging change caps out at +8.6% only at ~2300 armor) or requires a tuned armor value to reproduce what the amp reproduces exactly. The new value prices a sourced debuff the old value omitted.
